tools.description: Search Indian judgments and statutes: Supreme Court, High Courts, tribunals, central Acts. Up to 5 queries per call, merged and deduplicated, with AND, OR, NOT and "quoted phrases". Every word of a query must appear in the judgment, so a sentence finds only very long judgments: use 2 to 5 words courts use for the point (e.g. suppression material fact proposal form insurance), and several short queries rather than one long one. When the papers or the user name a case, search for it by name too; if the name doesn't return the judgment itself, find it through citator. For the leading authorities on a point, call citator with direction=cites on the newest relevant Supreme Court judgment, and direction=cited_by on a leading case for later ones. Filter by court in plain words ("SC", "Delhi HC", "all HCs"), type, dates, judge or title; sort by relevance or date. Every hit has an id for read_document. 20 credits per query per new page; 2 for your own repeat within 24 hours.

tools.description: Open judgments or statutes by id or citation ("(2017) 10 SCC 1", "s. 138 NI Act"). With no other field: an outline under 800 tokens with a map of issues, facts, arguments, reasoning and conclusion. Then read parts, a paragraph range, or find phrases inside the text; parts=["details"] gives metadata only. Up to 10 documents (50 for details). 3 credits to open a document for 7 days, then 1 credit per 4,000 tokens read; details 1 per id; a citation instead of an id 5.

tools.description: Who cited a judgment and how (relied on, negative, neutral), or what it cites, with the citing paragraph. Filter by treatment, court and year; output=file exports the whole cited-by set. Treatment labels are automated signals, not verdicts: read the paragraph. 20 credits per page of 10 rows; opening citing judgments for context costs as in read_document. For a research question, use both routes: direction=cites on the newest relevant Supreme Court judgment finds what it relies on; direction=cited_by on a leading case finds later cases applying it.

tools.description: Check every citation, quote and paragraph pinpoint in a draft before a human relies on it: SCC, SCC OnLine, AIR, SCR, INSC, Cri LJ and case names with a year. Says verified, wrong_paragraph, quote_not_found, ambiguous, not_found or unverifiable, with the closest passage. Up to 50 citations per call. 10 credits per citation checked plus 3 per judgment newly opened; 5 for one that doesn't resolve (not_found), or 10 when a case-name search ran for it; ambiguous ones are free.
